elements.content: Communication Goal: I can describe the steps of online shopping.

Lesson overview:
- Level: A0 General English
- Unit: Unit 7. Shopping
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: Shop online
- Materials: Website screenshots, step cards, order form, COSYmanuals 'imperatives' and 'present simple' pages.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• use e-commerce and online shopping vocabulary
• understand delivery and order confirmations
Recycling & Course Continuity:

Prior learning: Recycles shopping and payment vocabulary from Lesson 27.

Next lesson: Lesson 29 moves to age, health, and longevity.
Quick retrieval task: which words or phrases do you remember?
Which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

internet — the global computer network. Example: I use the internet every day.
order — a request to buy something. Example: I order my food online.
website — a page or group of pages online. Example: The website has good prices.
delivery — the arrival of something you ordered. Example: The delivery is on Friday.
online — on the internet. Example: I shop online.
basket — a container for shopping. Example: Put the items in your basket.
address — where you live. Example: Please write your address.
confirmation — a message that says something is complete. Example: I got an order confirmation.
buy — to get something with money. Example: I want to buy a gift.
pay — to give money for something. Example: I pay by card.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• I shop online. (talking about online shopping)
• I visit the website. (first step)
• I add items to my basket. (next step)
• I pay by card. (payment step)
• The delivery is on Friday. (talking about delivery)
• I get a confirmation. (order confirmation)
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'the global computer network'?
Which word means 'a request to buy something'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use imperatives to give instructions, directions, and advice.

Form:
Imperatives: Base verb + object: Open the door. Negative: Don't + base verb. Add 'please' to be polite.

Examples:
• Open your book, please.
• Turn left at the bank.
• Don't touch the screen.
• Click the link to order.
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
___ the door, please.
___ touch the screen.
___ left at the bank.
___ your name here.
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• ... (Open / Close / Click) the ...
• Don't ... (touch / open / click) the ...
• Please ... (turn / go / write) ...
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• How do you make a cup of tea? Give three instructions.
• How do you get to the station from here?
• What are three classroom instructions?
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write three instructions for using a phone.
• Write three instructions for making your favourite drink.
Reading: Shop online

I like to shop online. First, I visit the website. Then, I choose my items and add them to my basket. After that, I pay by card. I write my address and confirm the order. The delivery is on Friday. I get a confirmation by email. Online shopping is easy and fast!
What does the writer do first?
When is the delivery?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: How do I order online?
B: Visit the website and choose your items.
A: Then what?
B: Add them to your basket and pay by card.
A: When is the delivery?
B: It's on Friday. You get a confirmation by email.
What do you do after choosing items?
When is the delivery?
Speaking task: Explain the steps of online shopping to your partner. Then roleplay a delivery phone call.

• Do you shop online?
• What do you buy online?
• Is online shopping safe?
• Do you prefer online or in-store shopping?
• What do you do if the delivery is late?
Role-play: You ordered a gift online. Call customer service because the delivery is late.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write five instructions for online shopping using imperatives.
Model: Visit ... Choose ... Add ... Pay ... Wait for ...
